od_007_position: OD-007 is RATIFIED (Current Status: Ratified on 2026-07-17, ratified as specified). The approved option is Option 1 -- one-directional Citation: exactly one AIResponse, exactly one Evidence, no direct Evaluation write link. Evaluation traversal is `AIResponse -> Recommendation Artifact -> origin Issue -> Check Result/Evidence`. A read-model projection MAY denormalize that traversal but MUST NOT become write authority. Nothing in S-10 is withheld under OD-007.
ai_provider_gate_position: The `ai_assisted` path being unreachable at the Volume II baseline is SETTLED VOLUME I BEHAVIOUR, not a pending owner decision and not a withheld limb. `citation-policy-v1` states it directly: AI-assisted generation additionally requires active signed `ai-response-interim-v1` and `ai-safety-interim-v1` artifacts naming an approved provider adapter/model, data-handling approval, allowed Evidence Classifications, prompt-template hash, output schema, prohibited-content scanner and contract-review reference; no such provider artifact is bundled while provider, model and data-handling selection remains unapproved; therefore the deterministic interim behavior is `deterministic_template` generation from the exact catalog templates, and an `ai_assisted` request fails BEFORE entitlement reservation or provider call as `F1-AI-422 / ai_provider_unapproved`, creates no AIResponse or Citation, and may recover only by selecting deterministic generation or activating an approved signed artifact. No Owner Decision is pending on this: the register lists only OD-014, OD-023, OD-027, OD-031 and OD-032 as pending, and none of them is the AI provider gate. S-10 therefore contracts the COMPLETE AIResponse and Citation contract -- it is fully specified normative behaviour that the fail-closed gate protects -- plus the gate itself, and withholds nothing. An implementation MUST NOT choose a provider, send Evidence, or silently weaken this gate.
ownership_split_with_s_14: S-10 owns CAP-012: the AIResponse and Citation records, their fingerprints, lifecycles, claim manifest, coverage rule, validation transaction and the provider gate. S-14 owns WF-009 and CAP-016: Recommendation Artifact families, versions, templates, publication and the Current Recommendation Family Projection. The binding point is one-directional and named in both: a validated AIResponse binds to exactly one target Artifact version, and the Artifact governs its own publication. PRULE-015 is shared -- S-10 owns its CAP-012 limb (the response and scanner), S-14 owns its CAP-016 limb (deterministic template output).

MTX-012.interface_type: AI orchestration commands plus the tenant-scoped citation-validation service. CAP-012's Actor is the AI orchestration service, with an OrganizationAdmin or MarketingOperator for publication control. At the ratified baseline the generation limb is reachable only in `deterministic_template` mode; an `ai_assisted` request fails closed at the provider gate before entitlement reservation or provider call.
MTX-012.route: Not applicable - Volume I defines the commands, their permissions and their envelopes but no HTTP path, method or transport. Transport exposure is owned by API_CONTRACTS.md at the Volume II baseline. No inbound provider callback exists: the AIResponse lifecycle is driven by the orchestrating worker that made the request, so an inbound callback would be an unauthenticated surface with no authority behind it.
MTX-012.request_schema: AIResponse request: Organization and Project IDs, target `recommendation_id` and `artifact_version`, `origin_issue_id` and its state version, ordered input Evidence ID/content-digest/Validation-Decision tuples, prompt template ID/version, model ID/version, response-policy and citation-policy versions, locale, `request_fingerprint_sha256` with its retained preimage, idempotency key, and correlation ID.
MTX-012.response_schema: The AIResponse with its status, nullable rejection reason, the four due instants, immutable generated-payload reference and content digest, ordered claim manifest, state version and correlation ID; plus its Citations with their statuses and first-match reason codes. At the baseline an `ai_assisted` request returns `F1-AI-422 / ai_provider_unapproved` and no AIResponse record.
MTX-012.controller: Not applicable - no HTTP adapter is defined by Volume I; see route.
MTX-012.command: `Workflows::Wf009::RequestAiResponse`, `Workflows::Wf009::PersistGeneratedPayload`, `Workflows::Wf009::ProposeCitations`, `Workflows::Wf009::ValidateAiResponse` (the single validation transaction), `Workflows::Wf009::RejectAiResponse`, `Workflows::Wf009::ExpireAiResponse`, `Workflows::Wf009::SupersedeCitations`. `RequestAiResponse` is where the provider gate fires. Recommendation Artifact generation, versioning and publication are WF-009 commands owned by S-14.
MTX-012.command_input: As request_schema. The prompt envelope, when an approved signed artifact is later active, places immutable Evidence ONLY in a delimited untrusted-data field, never in system or developer instructions; strips executable markup and provider tool directives; sends no credentials, verification material, restricted Evidence or field above the artifact's classification allowlist; fixes the response to the exact Recommendation schema and claim manifest; and rejects unknown or extra fields.
MTX-012.command_output: Requested, generated, validated, rejected or expired AIResponse attempts and proposed, verified, invalid or superseded Citations with immutable claim and Evidence lineage, per CAP-012 Outputs.
MTX-012.actor: AI orchestration service identity for the request and generation limbs; the tenant-scoped citation-validation service for every Citation decision; an OrganizationAdmin or MarketingOperator holding `recommendation.publish` for publication control, which is S-14's command. A TechnicalImplementer is a consumer and cannot publish.
MTX-012.organization_scope: The origin Issue's Organization and Project. Every AIResponse, Citation and input Evidence record resolves inside it; the AIResponse carries Organization and Project IDs explicitly and the Citation carries them too.
MTX-012.aggregate: AIResponse as one root, Citation as a separate root belonging to exactly one AIResponse. RecommendationArtifact is the binding target and is a separate root owned by S-14; Issue and CheckResult are read-only antecedents.
MTX-012.aggregate_boundary: The validation transaction is the one bounded multi-root commit: one transaction persists a terminal decision for EVERY proposed Citation and changes the AIResponse to `validated` on full coverage or `rejected` on failure. Binding validated draft content to the target Artifact version happens only on full pass; on failure the rejected response and Citation decisions are retained for audit and no AI-assisted Artifact publishes. The AIResponse never writes to Evaluation: under OD-007 neither AIResponse nor Citation stores a direct Evaluation link.
MTX-012.value_objects: AiResponseId, RequestFingerprintSha256, RequestFingerprintPreimage, PromptTemplateId, PromptTemplateVersion, ModelId, ModelVersion, ResponsePolicyVersion, CitationPolicyVersion, ClaimKey, ClaimSha256, ClaimManifest, GeneratedPayloadDigest, GenerationDueAtUtc, ValidationDueAtUtc, PublicationExpiresAtUtc, CitationId, EvidenceLocator, CitationFingerprintSha256, CitationFingerprintPreimage, AiResponseStatus, CitationStatus.
MTX-012.domain_service: The tenant-scoped citation-validation service is named by Volume I and is the sole decider of every `proposed -> verified` and `proposed -> invalid` transition. It is not a convenience object: its identity is persisted on each Citation as the deciding service, so a Citation decision is attributable.
MTX-012.repository: `AiResponseRepository`, `CitationRepository`, `IssueRepository` read-only, `CheckResultRepository` read-only, `EvidenceRepository` read-only, `EvidenceValidationDecisionRepository` read-only, `RecommendationArtifactRepository` read-only at the binding boundary, `AiPolicyArtifactRepository` read-only for the signed `ai-response-interim-v1` and `ai-safety-interim-v1` artifacts.
MTX-012.persistence_model: `ai_responses` unique on `(organization_id, request_fingerprint_version, request_fingerprint_preimage)` -- the retained preimage, not `request_fingerprint_sha256`, is uniqueness authority, so the unique index MUST NOT be built on the hash alone. `citations` unique on the retained Citation preimage within one AIResponse, with `ai_response_id` NOT NULL, `evidence_id` NOT NULL and NO `evaluation_id` column at all: under OD-007 the absence is structural, not a nullable convenience. The generated payload is an immutable reference with a content digest; the claim manifest is ordered and immutable once generated. A same-hash/different-preimage record for either type never merges and holds its own row plus restricted collision telemetry.
MTX-012.migration: Not applicable at this row - the canonical schema owns `ai_responses` and `citations` per schemas/POSTGRESQL_SCHEMA.md. No product schema object is added. An `evaluation_id` column on either table MUST NOT be migrated: OD-007 ratified the one-directional model and a direct Evaluation write link is a prohibited transformation.
MTX-012.transaction_boundary: Request: one transaction creating or replaying the fingerprinted AIResponse at `requested`; at the baseline the provider gate rejects before this transaction opens, so no record is created. Generation: one transaction atomically persisting the generated payload, its digest, the ordered claim manifest and the proposed Citations. Validation: ONE transaction persisting a terminal decision for every proposed Citation, changing the AIResponse to validated or rejected, and binding draft content to the target Artifact version only on full pass. The `ai.generate` durable entitlement commit MUST commit strictly before `validation_due_at_utc`. No provider call sits inside a database transaction.
MTX-012.concurrency: The request fingerprint serializes the attempt: exact preimage replay returns the original attempt and never calls the provider or validates twice. Concurrent exact requests resolve to one attempt. The validation transaction is atomic over the complete Citation set, so a partially decided set is not observable. Publication atomically binds the validated AIResponse to the target Artifact version and cancels expiry; a bound response remains `validated` as immutable lineage. Entitlement reservation for `ai.generate` uses a 15-minute prestart lifetime and a 2-minute maximum execution with a 2-minute heartbeat, so a lost orchestrator releases rather than strands the unit.
MTX-012.idempotency: The AIResponse request-fingerprint preimage is canonical JSON containing exactly Organization, Project, target Recommendation and version, origin Issue and state version, ordered Evidence tuples, prompt template and version, model and version, response-policy and citation-policy versions, and locale. Exact preimage replay returns the original attempt with no provider call and no second validation. Reuse of its idempotency key with a DIFFERENT preimage is `idempotency_conflict`. A same hash with a different retained preimage never merges and emits restricted `AIResponseFingerprintCollision` telemetry. The Citation fingerprint preimage is canonical JSON containing exactly Organization, Project, AIResponse ID, Evidence ID with content digest and Validation Decision ID and status, claim key and digest, normalized evidence locator, and citation-policy version; within one AIResponse the full retained preimage is uniqueness authority, exact replay returns one Citation and one event outcome, and a same-hash/different-preimage record emits restricted `CitationFingerprintCollision` telemetry without merging.
MTX-012.background_job: `AiResponseGenerationWorker` per requested attempt, holding the `ai.generate` reservation lease; `AiResponseGenerationTimeoutJob` at `generation_due_at_utc`; `AiResponseValidationTimeoutJob` at `validation_due_at_utc`; `AiResponseExpiryJob` at `publication_expires_at_utc`. At the baseline none of these runs, because `RequestAiResponse` fails closed at the gate before an attempt exists.
MTX-012.queue: The AI generation queue, per the Volume I Background Processing action registry. Queue identity and worker topology are owned by BACKGROUND_PROCESSING.md; this row does not rename them.
MTX-012.retry_policy: Provider timeout and retry remain exactly those in the AIResponse lifecycle; NO hidden provider retry is allowed. A provider or validation retry creates a NEW AIResponse attempt linked by causation ID and never reopens a terminal response. `rejected` and `expired` are terminal. `ai_provider_unapproved` is nonretryable in the sense that recovery is selecting deterministic generation or activating an approved signed artifact, not re-submitting the same request.
MTX-012.terminal_failure: `requested -> rejected` for `generation_timeout`, `provider_failure` or `policy_denied`. `generated -> rejected` for `schema_invalid`, `citation_missing`, `citation_invalid`, `stale_input`, `prohibited_advisory_domain`, `policy_denied` or `validation_timeout`. Unpublished `validated -> expired`. These transitions are exhaustive. Rejected and expired are terminal; a corrected linkage is a new Citation and a corrected attempt is a new AIResponse.
MTX-012.reconciliation: One validation transaction ALWAYS persists a terminal decision for every proposed Citation, so no Citation is left proposed after validation. AIResponse rejection or validation timeout changes any remaining proposed Citation to `invalid` with `response_rejected` or `validation_timeout` in the same transaction. `verified -> superseded` with reason `artifact_version_superseded` occurs only when a later published Artifact version replaces the target version; invalid and superseded are terminal.
MTX-012.domain_events: `AIResponseRequested`, `AIResponseGenerated`, `AIResponseValidated`, `AIResponseRejected`, `AIResponseExpired`, `CitationProposed`, `CitationVerified`, `CitationInvalidated`, `CitationSuperseded`, restricted `AIResponseFingerprintCollision`, restricted `CitationFingerprintCollision`. `RecommendationArtifactGenerated`, `RecommendationPublished`, `RecommendationSuppressed` and `RecommendationRetired` are WF-009 Artifact events owned by S-14 and are not emitted here.
MTX-012.event_payload: The canonical envelope with the real `organization_id`, plus the AIResponse or Citation identity, target Recommendation and version, origin Issue and state version, prompt, model and policy versions, fingerprint outcome, claim key and digest for a Citation, the decision reason, the relevant due instant, and the correlation ID. Provider text, prompts, unrestricted responses, credentials and opaque error strings MUST NOT appear in any event payload or customer output; collision telemetry is restricted.
MTX-012.event_producer: `Workflows::Wf009` is the sole producer of the eleven events above. Provider latency, queue depth and lease state are technical telemetry and MUST NOT be emitted as domain events.
MTX-012.event_consumers: S-14 consumes the validated bound AIResponse as a publication predicate for an `ai_assisted` Artifact version, by reading it rather than by reacting to `AIResponseValidated`. No other consumer is named by Volume I.
MTX-012.serializer: Not applicable - no transport exposure is defined by Volume I; see route.
MTX-012.authorization_entry_point: The orchestration command, before mutation, and again at the `ai.generate` entitlement checkpoint immediately before the provider call. At the baseline the provider gate is evaluated BEFORE entitlement reservation, so a rejected `ai_assisted` request consumes no unit.
MTX-012.permission_checks: AI orchestration service identity for the request and generation limbs; the tenant-scoped citation-validation service identity for Citation decisions. `ai.generate` is the high-cost entitlement operation, counter group `ai.generate`, unit `validated_ai_response`, 1 unit, soft 20, hard 25, 15-minute prestart lifetime, 2-minute maximum execution, durable commit point `validated AIResponse is persisted for downstream use`. `recommendation.publish`, held by an OrganizationAdmin or MarketingOperator, governs publication and is S-14's check. Volume I defines no principal permission that reaches Citation validation, and none may be invented.
MTX-012.tenant_boundary: Organization and Project must match across the AIResponse, its target Artifact, its origin Issue, every input Evidence record and every Citation. `tenant_mismatch` is the FIRST reason in the Citation validation first-match order, so a cross-tenant Citation is rejected before any other check can mask it. The prompt envelope sends no credentials, verification material, restricted Evidence or field above the artifact's classification allowlist, and immutable Evidence is confined to a delimited untrusted-data field.
MTX-012.error_contract: Provider gate: `F1-AI-422 / ai_provider_unapproved`, before entitlement reservation or provider call, creating no AIResponse or Citation. AIResponse rejection reasons, exhaustive: `generation_timeout`, `provider_failure`, `policy_denied`, `schema_invalid`, `citation_missing`, `citation_invalid`, `stale_input`, `prohibited_advisory_domain`, `validation_timeout`. Output scanner first-match order, applied BEFORE Citation validation: `prompt_instruction_leakage`, `secret_or_personal_data`, `prohibited_advisory_domain`, `unsafe_external_action`, `output_schema_invalid`; any match changes the AIResponse to rejected with `policy_denied` EXCEPT the already canonical prohibited-advisory and schema reasons, publishes nothing, and permits only a new linked attempt after input or policy correction. Citation validation first-match order: `tenant_mismatch`, `claim_missing`, `claim_digest_mismatch`, `evidence_not_valid`, `evidence_digest_mismatch`, `locator_unresolved`, `evidence_not_in_origin_lineage`. Idempotency: `idempotency_conflict` on key reuse with a different preimage.
MTX-012.audit_record: Every AIResponse and Citation transition, collision, replay, timeout, coverage result and binding event, per CAP-012 Observability Requirements. Persisted: prompt, model and policy versions; response and Citation fingerprint preimages; the ordered claim manifest with claim keys and digests; the one-directional lineage; every decision with its deciding service identity and reason; and all timestamps, per CAP-012 Data Implications.
MTX-012.observability: Every AIResponse and Citation transition, collision, replay, timeout, coverage result and binding event. The four due instants are observable so an expiry is attributable to a clock boundary rather than to a lost attempt. At the baseline, every `ai_provider_unapproved` rejection is observable with its exact reason, so the gate firing is a visible fact rather than a silent absence.
MTX-012.retention: AIResponse and Citation records, their fingerprint preimages, claim manifests, decisions and timestamps are immutable lineage retained as `product_history`. The generated-payload reference is immutable. The retention window is owned by 015 DATA_LIFECYCLE.md; this row states none.

MTX-012.rollout: S-10 depends on S-09 for the origin Check Result's impact and confidence metadata and on S-12 for the eligible origin Issue; it gates S-14, which binds a validated AIResponse to a Recommendation Artifact version. Nothing is withheld: the provider gate is settled Volume I behaviour and the complete AIResponse and Citation contract is implemented behind it, so activating an approved signed artifact later requires configuration and its own controlled review rather than new contract work.

MTX-065.interface_type: Integrity rule over AI-assisted output. PRULE-014 governs CAP-012 and applies to WF-009. Its decision dependency OD-007 is RATIFIED. This row adds no command; it constrains the MTX-012 records.
MTX-065.route: Not applicable - PRULE-014 is a rule, not an interface.
MTX-065.request_schema: Not applicable - constrains the MTX-012 schema.
MTX-065.command: Enforced within `Workflows::Wf009::RequestAiResponse`, `ProposeCitations` and `ValidateAiResponse`. This row adds no command.
MTX-065.command_input: Not applicable - constrains the MTX-012 input.
MTX-065.command_output: Not applicable - constrains the MTX-012 output.
MTX-065.actor: AI orchestration service identity and the tenant-scoped citation-validation service; the rule constrains the records, not a principal.
MTX-065.organization_scope: The origin Issue's Organization and Project, carried explicitly on both records.
MTX-065.aggregate_boundary: The rule's one-parent clause is what fixes the boundary: exactly one AIResponse per Citation and exactly one Evidence per Citation. That, plus the absent Evaluation link, is why a Citation cannot be a join table and why evaluation traversal must go through the Artifact and the origin Issue.
MTX-065.value_objects: As MTX-012 - RequestFingerprintPreimage, CitationFingerprintPreimage, ClaimKey, ClaimSha256, EvidenceLocator, AiResponseStatus, CitationStatus.
MTX-065.domain_service: The tenant-scoped citation-validation service, as MTX-012. PRULE-014 names no other.
MTX-065.persistence_model: Not applicable as a new concept - PRULE-014 introduces no record. It constrains `citations`: `ai_response_id` NOT NULL with exactly one parent, `evidence_id` NOT NULL with exactly one target, and NO `evaluation_id` column; and `ai_responses`: the retained request-fingerprint preimage as uniqueness authority with the hash as an index only.
MTX-065.migration: Not applicable - no schema object is added. An `evaluation_id` column on `ai_responses` or `citations`, or a many-to-many join between Citation and AIResponse or Evidence, MUST NOT be migrated: OD-007 is ratified and a direct Evaluation write link is a prohibited transformation.
MTX-065.transaction_boundary: As MTX-012 - one fingerprinted attempt, one atomic generation transaction, one validation transaction that decides every proposed Citation.
MTX-065.concurrency: One fingerprinted AIResponse attempt per preimage: concurrent exact requests resolve to that attempt and neither calls the provider twice nor validates twice.
MTX-065.idempotency: Replay safety is the rule's own term. Exact preimage replay returns the original attempt; idempotency-key reuse with a different preimage is `idempotency_conflict`; a same-hash/different-preimage record never merges for either AIResponse or Citation and emits its restricted collision telemetry.
MTX-065.background_job: Not applicable - the rule constrains records, not workers. The lifecycle timers are MTX-012's.
MTX-065.queue: Not applicable - no queue of its own.
MTX-065.retry_policy: Not applicable - the rule defines no retry; it forbids the hidden one. Every provider timeout and retry is a named AIResponse transition, and a retry is a new attempt linked by causation ID.
MTX-065.terminal_failure: No incomplete response supplies published content. Only a validated, unexpired, bound response with complete verified coverage may supply an AI-assisted Artifact; a rejected or expired response is terminal and publishes nothing.
MTX-065.reconciliation: Exhaustive decisions and states is the rule's own clause: one validation transaction leaves no Citation proposed, and every AIResponse reaches exactly one of generated, validated, rejected or expired.
MTX-065.domain_events: Not applicable - PRULE-014 emits no event of its own; it constrains the eleven AIResponse and Citation events MTX-012 emits.
MTX-065.event_payload: Not applicable - no event of its own.
MTX-065.event_producer: Not applicable - no event of its own.
MTX-065.event_consumers: Not applicable - no event of its own.
MTX-065.authorization_entry_point: The orchestration and validation commands, before mutation; the rule is an integrity gate that runs in addition to, never instead of, the service-identity check.
MTX-065.permission_checks: Not applicable - PRULE-014 adds no permission. It binds every writer: no grant authorizes a Citation with two parents, a direct Evaluation link, or an uncovered claim.
MTX-065.tenant_boundary: `tenant_mismatch` is the first Citation validation reason, so a cross-tenant linkage is refused before any other check can mask it. Both records carry Organization and Project explicitly rather than inferring them from the Artifact.
MTX-065.error_contract: As MTX-012 - the exhaustive AIResponse rejection reasons and the seven-reason Citation first-match order, plus `idempotency_conflict`. PRULE-014 adds no reason of its own; its contribution is that the sets are exhaustive and ordered.

PRULE-015 governs CAP-012 and CAP-016 and applies to WF-009; its Decision Dependency is None. This row owns its CAP-012 limb -- the response, the scanner and the rejection path. MTX-066.command_output: Not applicable - constrains output content: a violating response publishes nothing.
MTX-066.actor: The AI orchestration service's output scanner and the Artifact validator; the rule constrains content, not a principal. It applies to BOTH generation modes, so a deterministic template is not exempt.
MTX-066.organization_scope: The origin Issue's Organization and Project.
MTX-066.aggregate: AIResponse for the CAP-012 limb; RecommendationArtifact for the CAP-016 limb owned by S-14.
MTX-066.aggregate_boundary: The rule crosses no boundary; it is a content predicate evaluated before publication on each root.
MTX-066.value_objects: AdvisoryScope fixed to `discoverability_only`, ScannerReasonCode, RejectionReason, GenerationMode.
MTX-066.domain_service: Not applicable - PRULE-015 names no domain service. The prohibited-content scanner is named by the signed `ai-safety-interim-v1` artifact and runs inside the validation command; the deterministic limb's check is a pure predicate over the rendered template.
MTX-066.repository: `AiResponseRepository`, `RecommendationArtifactRepository` read-only at this row's boundary, `AiPolicyArtifactRepository` read-only.
MTX-066.persistence_model: Not applicable - PRULE-015 introduces no persistent concept. It constrains the content of records MTX-012 and S-14's MTX-016 and MTX-034 write, and fixes `advisory_scope=discoverability_only` on every Artifact.
MTX-066.transaction_boundary: The scanner runs before Citation validation and inside the same validation transaction, so a violating response is never observable as validated. A rejected response and its Citation decisions are retained in that same transaction for audit.
MTX-066.concurrency: The predicate is a pure function of the rendered content, so concurrent evaluations agree. There is no race in which a violating response wins publication: publication requires validation, and validation applies the scanner first.
MTX-066.idempotency: A rejection under this rule is terminal for that attempt and is idempotent by the AIResponse's request fingerprint: replaying the identical request returns the same rejected attempt without rescanning or recalling the provider. Correction is a NEW linked attempt, not a re-decision.
MTX-066.background_job: Not applicable - the rule constrains a synchronous validation step, not a job.
MTX-066.queue: Not applicable - no queue of its own.
MTX-066.retry_policy: Not applicable - a `prohibited_advisory_domain` failure is NONRETRYABLE. Only a new linked attempt after input or policy correction is permitted.
MTX-066.terminal_failure: A personalized legal or tax conclusion, a compliance determination, a filing position, or an instruction to take a legal or tax action fails nonretryably with `prohibited_advisory_domain` in BOTH generated and deterministic output and publishes nothing. `advisory_scope` other than `discoverability_only` blocks publication.
MTX-066.reconciliation: The permitted boundary is precise and is the reconciliation rule: a Recommendation MAY state an observed discoverability fact and MAY direct the customer to consult a qualified professional; it MUST NOT supply the professional conclusion. Template rendering never introduces a legal or tax conclusion or a direct production mutation.
MTX-066.domain_events: Not applicable - PRULE-015 emits no event of its own; it gates `AIResponseRejected` with its reason and, on the S-14 limb, blocks `RecommendationPublished`.
MTX-066.event_payload: Not applicable - no event of its own.
MTX-066.event_producer: Not applicable - no event of its own.
MTX-066.event_consumers: Not applicable - no event of its own.
MTX-066.authorization_entry_point: The validation command, before the response can become validated. The rule is a content gate with no actor-facing entry point: no principal can approve prohibited content.
MTX-066.permission_checks: Not applicable - PRULE-015 adds no permission and grants no override. No actor, including one holding `recommendation.publish`, may publish a response that fails the scanner or carries a prohibited advisory conclusion.
